metric: IBM Data Engineering Professional Certificate
evidence: Each completed course is listed individually on /credentials with its own Coursera verification URL.

metric: Internal Smart India Hackathon 2026 qualification
caveat: The internal round, run by the university. This is not a claim of national-level selection.

metric: Software engineering internship, Motherson Technology Services
caveat: May to June 2026, on the AI/ML team. The work itself was on a private production codebase and cannot be shown.

metric: Public LinkedIn recommendations from Motherson colleagues
caveat: Written by the author's own manager and a senior engineer on the team, and reproduced on this site word for word.

metric: Open Source Lead, GitHub Community GITAM
caveat: A student community role held since August 2026, not an employment position.

metric: KAPS MedTech public deployment
caveat: The deployment is live and can be opened, seeded with demo accounts. A working deployment is not evidence that the system is production-ready.

metric: TripSync public deployment
caveat: Live and openable, and described by its own README as buggy and under active development.

metric: Automated test suite passing on Windows, Linux and macOS
caveat: The suite runs in GitHub Actions on all three platforms. It exercises disk images in simulation mode; it does not touch physical drives.

metric: X-platform classifier accuracy
method: Tuned XGBoost classifier over 64,919 labelled X accounts with 13 engineered features, evaluated on a held-out split of the same labelled corpus.
caveat: Measured on a held-out split of a public research dataset, not against live platform traffic. Reached only after removing a mislabelled 50,000-row subset that had capped accuracy at 67 percent.

metric: Meta/Instagram classifier accuracy
method: Tuned XGBoost classifier over 36,383 labelled Meta accounts with 7 engineered features, evaluated on a held-out split of the same labelled corpus.
caveat: Held-out evaluation on a public research dataset. The Meta feature set is smaller and the corpus is smaller, so the higher number than X does not mean the Meta problem was solved better.

metric: X-platform classifier F1 score
method: Same held-out evaluation split as the X accuracy figure, 64,919 labelled accounts, 13 features.
caveat: F1 sits well below accuracy, which is the honest reading of this model: it is less balanced on precision and recall than the headline accuracy suggests.

metric: Meta/Instagram classifier F1 score
method: Same held-out evaluation split as the Meta accuracy figure, 36,383 labelled accounts, 7 features.
caveat: A dataset figure, not a field figure. Nothing here has been evaluated against accounts the model had no corpus for.

metric: X-platform inference latency
method: Single-account inference through the tuned X model on the development machine, as recorded in the repository benchmark table.
caveat: Model inference only. It excludes live profile scraping, which dominates a real scan and is why the API client allows a 30-second timeout.

metric: Meta/Instagram inference latency
method: Single-account inference through the tuned Meta model on the development machine, as recorded in the repository benchmark table.
caveat: Model inference only, excluding scraping and the semantic layer. No concurrency or throughput figure was recorded.

metric: Labelled accounts in the training corpora
method: 64,919 X accounts plus 36,383 Meta accounts, drawn from public research datasets and assembled into two platform-specific feature matrices.
caveat: The labels are the research datasets' own judgements, not ground truth from the platforms. No measurement of drift between those corpora and current accounts exists.

metric: X-platform accuracy gained after removing mislabelled data
method: Accuracy before and after removing a mislabelled 50,000-row subset and splitting feature engineering into two platform-specific pipelines: 67 percent before, 90.04 percent after.
caveat: Two changes were made together, so the split between what the data removal bought and what the pipeline split bought was never isolated.

metric: NIST 800-88 Clear on a 512 MB disk image, including verification
method: Apple M4, disk image on the internal SSD, median of three runs, measured 2026-09-17 on macOS only. First run was 2.2 s.
caveat: This measures software overhead against a fast internal SSD. A physical USB drive is bound by its own write speed, and no run against one was recorded.

metric: DoD 5220.22-M on a 512 MB disk image
method: Apple M4, disk image on the internal SSD, median of three runs, measured 2026-09-17 on macOS only. First run was 11.4 s.
caveat: Software overhead on an internal SSD, macOS only. Windows and Linux timings were not taken.

metric: File eraser over 100 files of 64 KB
method: Apple M4, median of three runs, measured 2026-09-17. The same batch took 23.4 s before per-volume filesystem metadata was cached.
caveat: The improvement is a caching win on repeated work against one volume, not a faster overwrite. Small files on one volume is the case it was tuned for.

metric: pytsk3 recovery scan of a 128 MB FAT image
method: Apple M4, median of three runs, measured 2026-09-17. The deleted file was recovered byte-exact in 3 of 3 runs.
caveat: pytsk3 reads filesystem metadata, so this shows recovery while the metadata still exists. It says nothing about carving a file whose metadata is gone.

metric: PhotoRec recovery of a deleted text file from a 128 MB FAT image
method: Apple M4, median of three runs, measured 2026-09-17. PhotoRec took 0.28 s and returned the deleted text file in none of them, because a plain text file carries no signature to carve.
caveat: A negative result, published because it is the honest shape of signature carving. It is a limit of the approach for this file type, not a defect of the integration.

metric: Share of blocks read back during erase verification on a 1 TB drive
method: Verification reads a sample of blocks after each pass. The sample is 100 percent at 64 MB, 6 percent at 1 GB and 0.2 percent at 1 TB.
caveat: Verification coverage falls as the drive grows. On a large drive, a passing verification is a sampled result and is not evidence that every block was overwritten.

metric: Autocomplete lookup complexity
method: Trie traversal in C, one step per character, where k is the length of the query prefix. Lookup cost is therefore independent of the number of terms stored.
caveat: A complexity bound read off the implementation, not a timing. No wall-clock benchmark, dataset size or baseline comparison was recorded, and there is no public repository to inspect.

metric: Top-N suggestion ranking complexity
method: Min-heap priority queue over the candidate terms below the matched prefix node, keeping the N most frequent without a full sort pass.
caveat: A complexity bound, not a measured latency. No throughput figure exists and the code is not public.

metric: Memory leaks reported by Valgrind
method: Valgrind run over the project's own test cases against the C build, with manual heap management and allocation patterns chosen to limit fragmentation.
caveat: Clean on the project's own test cases only. There is no fuzzing run, no adversarial input set and no public corpus behind the result.

metric: Automated functional checks in the integration suite
method: A Node test runner covering input validation, rate limiting, duplicate protection, queue completion and resource isolation, run against a seeded database.
caveat: A count of checks, not a coverage figure. Nothing measures what fraction of the codebase they exercise, and there is no load or concurrency testing.

metric: CGPA, B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering, GITAM University
caveat: There is no public transcript to link. A reader who wants this checked should ask for the transcript directly.
evidence: Semester transcripts held by the author and stated on his resume and LinkedIn education entry. Not published, and therefore not verified.

metric: Reduction in data redundancy after schema normalisation
caveat: No before-and-after measurement was published alongside this figure, so it is recorded as the author's word rather than as a result.
evidence: Stated on the author's resume. The public repository does not contain the measurement or the dataset the figure was taken from.

metric: Time to initialise and seed a fresh KAPS environment
caveat: No timing was recorded and the figure depends on the database being reachable. The one-command setup script is real and in the repository; the number attached to it is not measured.
evidence: Stated on the author's resume. The repository ships the init_db.js script but publishes no timing.

metric: FastAPI module written from scratch for LegalLens chat history
caveat: The codebase is private to Motherson Technology Services and cannot be shown. The supporting evidence a reader can actually check is the public recommendation from the senior engineer who reviewed the work.
evidence: Stated on the author's resume. Corroborated in outline, though not by line count, in Ambuj Upadhyay's public LinkedIn recommendation.

metric: CRUD REST endpoints shipped for chat-session persistence
caveat: Private production codebase. Conversation recovery, archive and unarchive, title search and message save, coordinating Azure Blob writes with SQLite metadata.
evidence: Stated on the author's resume; the work is described independently in Ambuj Upadhyay's public LinkedIn recommendation.

metric: Bugs surfaced in a systematic codebase audit at Motherson
caveat: Including broken feature-type isolation across all three product modules. Written up as a 27-entry structured bug tracker that is internal to the company and not publishable.
evidence: Stated on the author's resume. The tracker itself is internal.

metric: NIST 800-88 Purge and firmware Secure Erase
caveat: The NVMe and ATA sanitize commands are generated as reference strings and are never executed by the application. Proving this would require running them against a drive whose firmware implements the command set, and confirming the outcome out of band rather than trusting the return code.

metric: Erase of a physical drive on any operating system
caveat: Every recorded erase was against a disk image. The platform matrix marks the physical-drive row untested on Windows, Linux and macOS alike. Proving it would require a recorded run against real removable media on each platform, with read-back verification and the elevated rights the operation needs.

metric: bulk_extractor artefact extraction
caveat: bulk_extractor is wired into the recovery pipeline but is installed neither on the development machine nor in CI, so that code path has never executed. Proving it would require installing the tool and recording an extraction against a corpus whose artefacts are known in advance.

metric: Recovery rate against a real forensic corpus
caveat: Recovery has only been observed on small purpose-built FAT disk images. The tool therefore has no recovery-rate figure to offer. Proving one would require running it against a published forensic corpus and reporting results per file type, including the cases it misses.

metric: Carving a deleted file with no filesystem metadata present
caveat: The recorded recovery result came through pytsk3, which reads filesystem metadata. No test exists that recovers a file once that metadata is gone. Proving it would require a disk image with the metadata destroyed and a byte-exact comparison against the original file.

metric: Bifragment gap carving of fragmented files
caveat: The implementation exists in reassembly.py but is called with attempt_gap_carving disabled, so it never runs. Built, not enabled. Proving it would require turning it on and recovering a deliberately fragmented file from an image built for the purpose.

metric: Partition-table recovery
caveat: Not implemented. TestDisk is not wired into the application at all. Proving it would first require building it, then recovering a partition table from an image whose table was deliberately damaged.

metric: Trusted RFC 3161 timestamping of audit entries
caveat: Absent from the application flow, which is why the audit log can prove the order of events but not when they happened. Proving it would require integrating a timestamp authority and validating the returned tokens against the hash chain.

metric: Precision and recall of the semantic threat analyser
caveat: The sentence-embedding threat layer is zero-shot and has never been scored against a labelled threat corpus, so it has no accuracy figure at all. Proving it would require a labelled set of threatening and benign posts and a reported precision and recall against it.

metric: Efficient support for multiple concurrent users
caveat: The author's resume states this and no measurement stands behind it. No load test was run and no request rate was recorded. Proving it would require a benchmark against the deployed API at a stated concurrency, reporting latency and error rate.

metric: Sub-second cold start from the serialised index
caveat: The binary serialisation format exists so that start is a read rather than a rebuild, but no start-up timing was ever recorded. Proving it would require timing a cold start at a stated index size, against the rebuild time it is meant to replace.
